This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**13** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via record_id (symbol, a field of const object EMPTY_VALUE; a field of const object TYPE_NOUN), record_id (literal, a string literal in defaultMatches))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `defaultValue (literal, 41 pages)`
- **16** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d62d973734d1e0af3f183340a5674f320b7c0858` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9c56ff111a777edb73bceb1f01bdc38a9791609a` — the merge of head `bb33ace7a2c8a9d1443d088873c8d9b9bbb60889` into base `d62d973734d1e0af3f183340a5674f320b7c0858`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9c56ff111a777edb73bceb1f01bdc38a9791609a && git checkout 9c56ff111a777edb73bceb1f01bdc38a9791609a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d62d973734d1e0af3f183340a5674f320b7c0858 bb33ace7a2c8a9d1443d088873c8d9b9bbb60889 && git checkout -B drift-repro d62d973734d1e0af3f183340a5674f320b7c0858 && git merge --no-ff bb33ace7a2c8a9d1443d088873c8d9b9bbb60889

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d62d973734d1e0af3f183340a5674f320b7c0858
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d62d973734d1e0af3f183340a5674f320b7c0858` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bb33ace7a2c8a9d1443d088873c8d9b9bbb60889`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-page-variables.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.app-nav-visible-predicate-writes.test.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.page-variable-writes.test.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.page-visibility-predicate-writes.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-predicate-path-refs.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.runtime-surface.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.draft-publish-verdict.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts + packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/expression.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/metadata-collection.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts, packages/lint/src/collection-entries.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rule-wiring.test.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts, ui/packages/core/src/evaluator/ExpressionEvaluator.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/providers/ExpressionProvider.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useNavMemberGates.ts, ui/packages/react/src/hooks/usePageVariables.tsx, ui/packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts, examples/app-crm/src/apps/crm.app.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/page-variables.page.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/contact-form.page.ts. Not reviewed (prose faces): the changeset and the four content/docs transcripts, read for ② only.

Check-runs on the head at review time: 62 runs, 0 failed, 0 cancelled, 27 still in progress (Test Core 1-8, Test UI 1-16, Build Core, Build Docs, Live E2E UI, the five Type Check jobs, the six Lint jobs still running). Completed green: Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Build UI Deps, Plan Test Core shards. The pending families are the queue guard's to wait on; nothing in this record re-runs or pre-judges them.

### ① Derived judgments

1. App writes: a `navigation[].visible`, `areas[].navigation[].visible` or any `children[].visible` that is a bare string or a `{ dialect: 'cel', source }` envelope and does not parse on formula's `parseCelToAstWithReason` is now refused with `visibility-predicate-syntax` at the key path. RIGHT. The spec declares the slot as `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema` (app.zod.ts line 371), whose string arm is by definition `{ dialect: 'cel', source }` (expression.zod.ts lines 269-274), and the console reads both shapes on the CEL engine (ExpressionEvaluator.ts `evaluateCondition`, the #27457 branch) and WITHHOLDS the entry on a fault (ExpressionProvider.tsx `evaluateNavigationVisibility`, `throwOnError` then `withhold`). The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real at the author; nothing the console could ever render is taken away.
2. App writes: a `${...}` template bare string on a nav `visible` is now refused too, since it is not CEL. RIGHT, named as the one console-tolerated shape the door now closes: the console still routes a `${` string to its legacy path, but the spec never declared that reading (bare string = CEL), the page `visibleWhen` door has refused the same spelling since #6253 with the same `celRefusal`, and the corpus (examples, platform packages, docs, skills) carries no `${` nav `visible`. Parity, not a new refusal class.
3. App writes: a boolean `visible`, an envelope of dialect `template` or `cron`, and an envelope without a string `source` are not judged. RIGHT. The spec admits every dialect envelope on this slot; the console evaluates a non-cel envelope on its legacy path; an envelope without `source` is already the spec parse's refusal (`EVALUATED_EXPRESSION_SOURCE_REQUIRED`). The rule narrows nothing the spec leaves open.
4. App writes: only the syntax verdict runs on a nav entry; the family's root-binding verdicts (`visibility-bare-identifier`, `visibility-root-mislayered`, `visibility-predicate-unknown-function`, `has()` shape) do not. RIGHT by measurement: the shell binds `current_user`, `user`, `ctx.user`, `os.user`, `features` and `data` beside a `dataSource` (ExpressionProvider.tsx line 213; useNavMemberGates.ts `navEntryVisible`), not `record` or `page`, so the page-rooted checks would refuse `features.cloudManaged != true` and `current_user.can('crm_opportunity', 'read')`, both of which the console evaluates. The PR's control list pins exactly these.
5. `validatePredicatePathRefs` declares `app` beside its sibling and judges nothing on an app write. RIGHT: `authoring-rule-wiring.test.ts` pins the family on one `runtimeTypes` set (lines 469-497), and the rule walks `stack.views` only; the pin in `validate-predicate-path-refs.test.ts` is updated with the reason.
6. The app door's `rulesRun` disclosure grows from `[validateSecurityRoleWord]` to `[validateVisibilityPredicates, validatePredicatePathRefs, validateSecurityRoleWord]`; the two pins in `validate-security-posture.runtime-surface.test.ts` are updated. RIGHT, additive on a 422 or 2xx wire detail; no other test at head enumerates the app door's list (grepped).
7. Page writes: `page-variable-name-duplicate` (located at the later entry, naming the first index), `page-variable-name-empty` (empty or blank), `page-variable-default-type` (a present, non-null `defaultValue` whose JS kind is not the declared `type`'s: string for `string` and `record_id`, finite number, boolean, plain object, array; an absent `type` is judged as `string`). RIGHT against the spec and the consumer: `PageVariableSchema` (page.zod.ts lines 895-915) declares `type` with `.default('string')` and `defaultValue: z.unknown()`, so the untyped-number refusal follows the declared default, not the rule's invention; the console's `initializeVariables` (usePageVariables.tsx lines 40-69) seeds `defaultValue` as written when present (`null` included, so admitting `null` matches what the consumer does), falls to `''` for `string`, `record_id` and anything else, and keeps the LAST of two same-named declarations. `record_id` as a string is consistent with the spec's own typing of record ids on UI surfaces (`recordId: z.string()`, component.zod.ts line 2524). Types outside the enum are the parse's refusal and are left alone. The two showcase pages (5 variables) are admitted by the control set.
8. Public surface of `@objectstack/lint`: `validatePageVariables`, the three id constants and `PageVariableFinding` are exported from index.ts; three `os explain` entries and a nav paragraph on `visibility-predicate-syntax` are added. RIGHT; the explanation entries meet the registry's own pins (`covers` under 60 chars without a period, paragraphs naming no issue number).
9. `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` rule count 57 to 58 in the four CLI transcripts. RIGHT (the registry derives it; `check:docs-transcript-drift` is the gate).
10. One implementation at every surface, verified in the live tree: the metadata save door (`judgeRuntimeAuthoringRules` to `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate` to `runRuntimeAuthoringRules`, which filters `AUTHORING_RULES` by `runtimeTypes` and builds the snapshot with `TYPE_TO_STACK_KEY.app = 'apps'`, `page = 'pages'`), the draft `_diagnostics` (`draftPublishVerdict` calls the same judge with `state: 'active'`), the publish (`assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` is the same judge plus the throw) and the CLI (`runAuthoringRules('validate')` over `normalizeStackInput`, which coerces map collections to arrays and leaves nav `visible` and page `variables` as authored). No gate source in `metadata-protocol` moves; the protocol tests pin the draft read, the publish 422 and the active save. Nothing stored keeps its stored shape changed: a stored app or page keeps loading; only its next save is judged.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28663-nav-visible-syntax-page-variables.md`: `@objectstack/lint` **minor**, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `Skills-docs: none` with its reason, and one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with the no-conversion argument. Matches what the diff publishes: a value the author could write is now refused at every door (narrowed), on the one package the diff moves (`metadata-protocol` changes are tests only, which publish nothing). The `(narrowing)` arm is the BREAKING one by AGENTS.md's declaration rule, and the kind takes at least minor. The PR body carries the same two lines. `Check Changeset` and the PR-body guards are green on the head. Clause-②: `no (narrowing)` is right, and the claim comment's bare `no` is the seat's own line to amend (③ item 1).

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared.

Deviations, each answered:
1. Claim line `Clause-②: no` versus PR body and changeset `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Answered: the PR body and changeset are the records the gates read and they are right; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` refuses `narrowed` beside a line without the arm. The seat amends its claim comment; no PR change.
2. File surface widened to four `content/docs/**` CLI transcripts and four existing lint test pins. Answered: the transcripts are the mechanical rule-count line `check:docs-transcript-drift` enforces, not teaching prose; the four pins are the app and page doors' rule lists, which any registry change must re-pin. Both inside the ruling's intent; nothing under `packages/spec/**`, `packages/formula/**` or `ui/**` is touched.

Out-of-scope findings the dev reported, each escalated rather than fixed here:
3. A page variable `source` naming a component the page does not hold is still admitted. The card's item 2 lists it, its Expected line does not, and the ruling names uniqueness, name and default-versus-type only. Escalated: the seat files it (class a, dedupe words given in the report).
4. A `visibleWhen` reading an undeclared `page.X` is still admitted. Same disposition; the seat files it.
5. A nav `visible` that is flawless CEL over the parse budget is still admitted. See ④ S1; the seat files it.
6. The operator-table hint on a nav entry carries a record-rooted example. See ④ S2.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main` and the consumer that evaluates it: the spec already says a nav `visible` is CEL and an evaluated slot must be something the engine runs; the console's navigation gate falls closed on a fault. A predicate that cannot parse therefore never worked for any viewer, and refusing it at the author is the spec's own refusal made real, not a capability withdrawn. The page-variable rule judges a list the spec types entry-by-entry and never judged as a list; each verdict mirrors what `usePageVariables` does with the declaration (last wins, unreachable name, wrong-kind seed), so no declared variable shape that the console honours is refused. Attempts to break it: every shape the console evaluates on a nav entry (`current_user.can(...)`, `features.*`, `user.isPlatformAdmin == true`, the `in` membership test, the cel envelope, a boolean, a template envelope) is admitted at both doors by the PR's controls and by reading `celRefusal` (blank source answers null, bounds answers a kind the nav walker drops, only `syntax` fires); the single nav `visible` in the shipped corpus (`examples/app-crm`) and the five showcase variables pass; map-shaped `apps` collections resolve through `collectionEntries` with honest paths; a non-record nav entry or a non-array `navigation`/`variables` is skipped, never thrown on. The differential at the door is clean because `apps` and `pages` are not context collections, so the written item's own findings are the only ones that can appear.

Findings:
- S1 (should-fix, follow-up card): a nav `visible` that is valid CEL but over `DEFAULT_LIMITS` is admitted at every door, while the console's engine refuses it at parse under the same limits and the nav gate withholds the entry, which is the card's silent-disappearance shape by another route. `celRefusal` already returns `kind: 'bounds'`; `walkNavPredicates` drops it, so the fix is a second arm with the existing `visibility-predicate-over-budget` id and the nav consequence clause. Not a must-fix here: the ruling names the syntax judgment alone and the dev reported the gap for filing.
- S2 (should-fix, cosmetic): when a nav entry uses an other-language operator (`===`), the hint's example comes from the shared operator table and is `record`-rooted; the `SyntaxSurface.example` is read only on the no-token branch. The operator correction itself is right; a per-surface example on the token branch would finish the job.
- S3 (should-fix, by filing): the two page-variable faults the card observed and the ruling left out (unknown `source` component, undeclared `page.X` read) stay admitted; the seat files them as reported.
- Must-fix: none.

**VERDICT: PASS**
